title: Phone call: baby with diarrhoea and vomiting

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Hello, is that Freya's mum?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Yes, it's Leanne.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Hi Leanne, it's Dr Mistry calling back from the surgery. Are you able to talk?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Yes, she's on my lap.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Can you confirm Freya's date of birth?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Fourteenth of December. She's ten months.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Thank you. What's been happening?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: She started being sick last night, and then diarrhoea this morning.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How many times has she been sick?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: About five times since last night. Less today.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: What colour is the sick? Is it ever green?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: No, it's milky. Just her milk coming back.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How many dirty nappies?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Six or seven runny ones today.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any blood in them?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: No. Her brother had blood in his last week when he had the same thing, but there's none in hers.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Her brother's had a similar illness?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Yes, he got it at nursery. Freya goes to the same nursery.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Okay. How about wet nappies today?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: About four, I think. Oh, wait, no. I've only changed two wet ones since this morning. The others were dirty.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Two wet nappies since this morning. And it's now about two o'clock. Is she drinking?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: She's having little bits of milk. She's breastfed and she has a bit of formula.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Has she had a temperature?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: 37.4 this morning.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How is she in herself? Is she alert, playing?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: She's grumpy, but she's watching the telly and playing with her blocks.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Is she very sleepy or floppy, or hard to wake?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any rash?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any medical problems? Medicines? Allergies?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: No, she's well normally. No medicines, no allergies.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: I can't examine her over the phone. It sounds like gastroenteritis, a tummy bug, probably the same one her brother had. Most babies get better within a few days.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: But I'm a bit concerned that she's only had two wet nappies today, so I'd like to see her this afternoon. Can you bring her in at four o'clock?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Yes, I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: In the meantime, keep breastfeeding her, and give small amounts of oral rehydration solution, like Dioralyte, a teaspoon every few minutes.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: If she becomes floppy, very sleepy or hard to wake, or gets a rash that doesn't fade when you press a glass on it, call 999.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: If her sick goes green, or you see blood in her nappy, take her to A&E.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Okay. Thank you, I'll see you at four.

reference_note.presenting_complaint: Vomiting and diarrhoea in a 10-month-old since last night.
reference_note.history: About five non-bilious, milky vomits since last night, fewer today. Six to seven loose stools today. No blood in Freya's stools (her brother had blood in his stool with a similar illness last week). Brother had similar illness from nursery; Freya attends the same nursery. Two wet nappies since this morning (initially said four). Taking small amounts of breast milk and formula. Temperature 37.4 °C. Alert and playing. Not drowsy or floppy. No rash. Previously well.
reference_note.medications_allergies: No regular medications. No known drug allergies.
reference_note.impression: Probable viral gastroenteritis with reduced urine output.
reference_note.plan: Face-to-face assessment at the surgery today at 16:00. Continue breastfeeding; oral rehydration solution in small, frequent amounts.
reference_note.safety_netting: Call 999 if floppy, very sleepy, hard to wake, or non-blanching rash. Attend A&E if green vomit or blood in stool.
